a unit arc with constant sides has `ℓ ≤ 60°` (its ends lie in the closure of one tile)

at `ℓ = 60°` **both** side tiles lie in the lens `B̄(A, 1) ∩ B̄(B, 1)`: `T_in ⊆ Reul(P, A, B)`, `T_out ⊆ Reul(A, B, C) ∖ B̄(P, 1)`, `C = A + B − P`; at each end their sectors lie in the two corner cones (120° and 60°), which fill exactly the closed half-plane facing the other end, so each end is a vertex carrying a third tile

for a blade `t_{j+1}` whose clockwise edge `j` is shorter than 60°: every 5/6 tile bordering its counter-clockwise side `M_j` (from `q_j` to `w_{j+1}`) is one tile `μ_j`, and every 5/6 tile bordering the inside part of its clockwise side `L_j` is one tile of the other colour; so `w_{j+1} ∈ cl μ_j`

outside E2 the tile bordering `t_{j+1}`'s side `M_j` also borders the whole inside part of `t_{j+2}`'s side `L_{j+1}` (`μ_j = Λ_{j+1}`)

at each centre `q_k`, outside E1 and E2: either (B) `α_k = 60°` and `μ_{k−1} ∋ q_k`, or (A) `t_{k+1}` borders the ring clockwise from `q_k` for `λ_k ∈ [α_k − 60°, 60°]`, the outside tile there has colour `k − 1`, and `α_{k−1} + α_k ≤ 180°`; so every cone is at most `120°`
